paragraph:
The price of being discovered
A mountain village learns that popularity is easier to attract than to govern

In the fictional, (landlocked) republic of Arven, the mountain village of Tessel has become an online sensation. Photographs show (serried) peaks, (striated) cliffs and a (serrated) skyline. The tourism board promises an (unspoiled) refuge. The bus park is already (packed). For the (uninitiated), the difference can be startling.

The change is (marked). A once (depressed) local economy now sells rooms at metropolitan prices. Officials hail an (untapped) resource finally recognised. Yet a landscape is not an idle factory: extracting more income from it can alter the thing visitors came to see. The village's formerly (settled) routines are already disappearing.

Along the old footpath, (dappled) light falls across a (gnarled) tree. A (pied) bird watches a (brindled) dog investigate a picnic basket. The village photographer jokes that every (biped) now has a camera and every (quadruped) a social-media account. The joke is becoming a business plan.

A (celebrated) travel presenter supplied the decisive endorsement. His (well-groomed) appearance contrasted with the shepherd beside him, whose (wizened) face became the campaign's emblem. The shepherd was paid once. The video continues to earn money, illustrating a distinction between being visible and having bargaining power.

The campaign celebrates supposedly (untutored) wisdom while selling highly (sophisticated) hospitality. A hotel describes its menu as an (acquired) taste and its furnishings as (understated). It charges extra for both. Visitors seem (impressed), although it is unclear how much of their enthusiasm survives the invoice.

At lunch, a waiter offers (vinegared) vegetables with a four-(tined) fork. The meal leaves one guest (satiated); another declares himself (sated) with rustic authenticity. Neither asks why the kitchen staff live beyond the valley. Their experience of simplicity requires somebody else's complicated commute.

The investor behind the largest hotel has a (checkered) record. He is (enamored) of Tessel's charm and rather less attached to its planning limits. His proposal would convert a (dilapidated) school into suites. The building would be (restored), but the village would lose a possible site for childcare.

The council's own accounts offer little comfort. It is heavily (indebted), its transport budget (bloated) by emergency contracts. An (antiquated) booking system still depends on a (superannuated) computer. Modernisation is overdue, but a new screen cannot decide how many coaches a narrow road should carry.

At a meeting, the mayor delivers an (impassioned) defence of growth. A (seasoned) clerk supplies a more (unimpassioned) account of sewage capacity. The numbers have been (verified). Her conclusion is not that tourism must end, but that expansion without infrastructure cannot be (sustained).

That distinction is quickly lost. A (garbled) summary circulates online, followed by accusations that officials despise visitors. Residents already (inflamed) by noise interpret a (mistimed) promotional launch as provocation. A (muffled) apology from the back of the meeting hall satisfies nobody.

The mayor is usually (even-tempered), but a hostile question leaves him (flustered). He regains a (composed) expression and offers a (measured) reply. This is useful. His next assurance—that benefits are effectively (assured)—is less so. Confidence is not a substitute for a distribution plan.

Tourism's gains are uneven. Owners can raise rents; workers face higher living costs. Demand is approaching a (saturated) peak on summer weekends, while winter trade remains weak. A system of (graduated) visitor charges might fund services, provided its purpose and limits are clearly (defined).

The alternative is an (unregulated) scramble for bookings. A (calculated) decision to exceed a permit is different from an (unpremeditated) mistake, just as (premeditated) deception differs from confused paperwork. Enforcement should distinguish them. It should not reward whichever operator can appear most bewildered.

Some residents have become (resigned) to losing familiar shops. Others retain an (unfeigned) enthusiasm for newcomers. A café owner's welcome is not necessarily (feigned) because it also earns revenue. Mixed motives are normal; a village need not choose between sainthood and commerce.

There is, however, an (ingrained) habit of treating dissent as ignorance. The hotelier calls opponents (unenlightened); opponents call him (unprincipled). Neither label explains the financing. An (informed) discussion would examine water use, housing and public costs before judging anybody's character.

Local folklore offers distractions. A summer play features a (henpecked) innkeeper, a (wicked) landlord and two (star-crossed) lovers. Its performance is so (mannered) that a critic calls the comedy (labored). On stage, simple villains are convenient. In a planning hearing, they are usually evasions.

The same critic makes matters worse by describing a protest as (lowbred). Such contempt is (unjustified). A resident can be (opinionated) without being wrong, and an argument can be (animated) without being dangerous. Civility should improve the discussion, not exclude those lacking polished accents.

The valley also contains places that locals regard as (sacred). Their attachment is not reducible to ticket revenue. A (cultivated) appreciation of scenery may coexist with obligations to family and memory; visitors can feel a (kindred) affection without acquiring ownership. Access requires negotiation rather than sentimental entitlement.

An old farm ledger makes the point. Its (maculated) pages record floods, repairs and debts. Tessel has never (possessed) the effortless prosperity pictured in advertisements. A path (marred) by erosion is evidence of work deferred, not merely an opportunity for a dramatic photograph.

One storm brings those omissions into focus. A fallen branch leaves a shelter (shattered); an (improvised) shuttle strands passengers at the wrong stop. A (disheveled) guide spends the evening finding them rooms. The incident is costly, but calling it an (unmitigated) disaster obscures the competence that prevented something worse.

The guide has long been (inured) to sudden changes. This time she feels (dejected), while guests are understandably (agitated). A manager, visibly (discombobulated), first blames the weather and then his employees. Staff have (repressed) their complaints for months. A review that ignores them will miss the most useful evidence.

The council's response is (belated), but potentially valuable. It commissions a joint transport and housing plan, with assumptions open to scrutiny. Its initial optimism is (deflated), and the investor's enthusiasm is (damped) by more realistic costs. Neither development is a reason for despair.

The resulting agreement leaves all parties (constrained). The hotel gets fewer rooms; the council funds reliable buses; residents accept a limited extension. Not every complaint is upheld, and several allegations remain (unsubstantiated). Compromise works by specifying obligations, not by manufacturing unanimity.

Tessel's leaders have (underestimated) the effort required to manage popularity. They are still (infatuated) with visitor numbers and easily (distracted) by publicity. But the data now (collected) could support better decisions. A council (disposed) to learn should welcome that opportunity.

The choice is not between isolation and (unbridled) growth. It is between treating a village as a place people inhabit and treating it as a picture people purchase. Tessel can remain attractive without pretending it can accommodate everyone. The first sign of maturity would be an advertisement that admits as much.
translation:
被发现的代价
一座山村发现，吸引人气比管理人气容易

在虚构的(内陆)共和国阿尔文，山村特塞尔成了网络热门。照片展示着(密集排列的)山峰、(带条纹的)峭壁和(锯齿状的)天际线。旅游局承诺，这是一处(未遭破坏的)避世之地。旅游大巴停车场却早已(挤得满满当当)。对于(不知内情的人)，这种落差可能令人吃惊。

变化十分(显著)。曾经(萧条的)地方经济，如今以大都市的价格出售客房。官员欢呼，一项(尚未开发的)资源终于获得认可。然而，景观并不是闲置工厂：从中获取更多收入，可能改变游客原本想看的东西。村庄昔日(安定的)生活节奏已经开始消失。

老步道旁，(斑驳的)阳光落在一棵(盘根错节的)树上。一只(杂色的)鸟看着一条(虎斑的)狗翻查野餐篮。村里的摄影师开玩笑说，如今每个(两足动物)都有相机，每个(四足动物)都有社交媒体账号。这句笑话正在变成商业计划。

一位(著名的)旅游节目主持人带来了决定性的推荐。他(仪容整洁的)外表，与身旁牧羊人形成对照；后者(干瘪多皱的)脸成了宣传活动的标志。牧羊人只拿到一次报酬，视频却继续赚钱。这说明，被人看见与拥有议价能力，是两回事。

宣传一边赞美所谓(未经教导的)智慧，一边出售高度(精致复杂的)接待服务。一家酒店称，它的菜单需要(后天培养的)品味，陈设则讲究(低调含蓄)。两者都要额外收费。游客似乎(印象深刻)，只是收到账单后，这份热情还能剩下多少，并不清楚。

午餐时，侍者用一把四(齿的)叉子配上(醋腌的)蔬菜。一位客人吃得(心满意足)，另一位则宣称自己已经(充分满足于)乡村的真实感。两人都没问，为什么厨房员工住在山谷之外。他们体验到的简单生活，需要别人复杂的通勤来支撑。

最大酒店背后的投资者有着(好坏参半的)经历。他(迷恋)特塞尔的魅力，却没那么珍惜当地规划限制。他提议把一所(破败的)学校改成套房。建筑会得到(修复)，但村庄也会失去一处可能用于托育的场所。

议会自己的账目同样令人不安。它(负债累累)，交通预算因紧急合同而(膨胀)。一套(陈旧的)预订系统仍依赖一台(老旧淘汰的)电脑。现代化早该进行，但新屏幕无法决定一条窄路究竟能容纳多少辆大巴。

在一次会议上，村长为增长作出(慷慨激昂的)辩护。一位(经验丰富的)办事员则以更(不动感情的)方式说明污水处理能力。数字已经得到(核实)。她的结论并非必须终结旅游，而是缺乏基础设施的扩张无法(持续)。

这一区别很快被忽略。一份(歪曲混乱的)摘要在网上流传，随后出现官员轻视游客的指控。居民本已被噪声(激怒)，把一场(时机不当的)宣传启动活动视为挑衅。会场后方传来一句(含混低沉的)道歉，谁也不满意。

村长通常(性情平和)，但一个敌意问题让他(慌乱)。他重新摆出(镇定的)表情，给出(审慎的)回应。这很有用。随后他又保证，收益实际上是(有保障的)，这就没那么有用了。信心不能代替收益分配方案。

旅游业的收益并不均匀。业主可以提高租金，工人却面对更高的生活成本。夏季周末，需求接近(饱和的)峰值，冬季生意依然疲弱。一套(分级的)游客收费制度，或许能够资助公共服务，前提是目的与边界得到清楚(界定)。

另一种选择，是(不受监管的)抢单竞争。有意超出许可的(蓄意的)决定，不同于(未经预谋的)错误；正如(预谋的)欺骗，不同于文书混乱。执法应当区分这些情况，而不是奖励最会装糊涂的经营者。

一些居民已经(无奈接受)熟悉商店的消失。另一些人则对新来者保持(真诚的)热情。咖啡馆老板的欢迎，不会仅仅因为也能赚钱，就必然是(假装的)。动机混合很正常，村庄不必在圣洁与商业之间二选一。

然而，把异议当成无知，是一种(根深蒂固的)习惯。酒店老板称反对者(不开明)，反对者则称他(毫无原则)。两种标签都没有解释融资问题。一场(有充分依据的)讨论，应先考察用水、住房和公共成本，再判断任何人的品格。

地方民间故事提供了转移注意力的材料。夏季戏剧里，有一位(惧内的)旅店老板、一位(邪恶的)地主，以及一对(命运多舛的)恋人。表演如此(矫揉造作)，以至于一位评论家称这出喜剧(生硬费力)。舞台上，简单的反派很方便；规划听证会上，他们往往只是逃避问题的借口。

同一位评论家又把一场抗议描述为(粗鄙的)，使事情更糟。这种轻蔑(毫无道理)。居民可以(固执己见)却并没有错，争论也可以(热烈)而不危险。文明礼貌应当改善讨论，而不是排除那些口音不够优雅的人。

山谷还有一些被当地人视为(神圣的)地方。他们的依恋不能折算成门票收入。对景观(有修养的)欣赏，可以与家庭和记忆的责任并存；游客也能产生(相近的)感情，却不会因此获得所有权。进入这些地方需要协商，而不是凭感情索取特权。

一本旧农场账簿说明了这一点。(污迹斑斑的)书页记录着洪水、维修和债务。特塞尔从未(拥有)广告里那种毫不费力的繁荣。一条被侵蚀(损坏的)小路，是维护工作遭到拖延的证据，而不只是拍摄戏剧性照片的机会。

一场暴风雨让这些疏漏变得明显。掉落的树枝使一处遮蔽棚(破碎毁坏)，一班(临时拼凑的)接驳车把乘客丢在错误站点。一位(衣发凌乱的)导游整晚替他们寻找房间。事件代价不小，但称之为(彻头彻尾的)灾难，会掩盖那些避免更坏结果的专业能力。

导游早已(习惯忍受)突发变化。这一次，她感到(沮丧)，客人也理所当然地(焦躁不安)。一位明显(晕头转向的)经理先怪天气，再怪员工。员工已经(压抑)抱怨数月。忽视他们的复盘，将错过最有用的证据。

议会的回应虽然(姗姗来迟)，却可能有价值。它委托制定交通与住房联合计划，并公开假设供人审查。最初的乐观被(打消)，投资者的热情也被更现实的成本(抑制)。这两种变化都不是绝望的理由。

最终协议让各方都受到(约束)。酒店获得的客房数减少，议会资助可靠的公交服务，居民接受有限扩建。并非所有投诉都成立，几项指控仍(未经证实)。妥协靠明确义务发挥作用，而不是靠制造全体一致。

特塞尔的领导者(低估了)管理人气所需的努力。他们仍(痴迷于)游客数量，也容易被宣传(分散注意力)。但如今(收集到的)数据，可以支持更好的决策。一个(愿意)学习的议会，应当欢迎这种机会。

选择并不是隔绝与(无拘无束的)增长之间的二选一，而是把村庄视为人们生活的地方，还是人们花钱购买的一幅图景。特塞尔可以保持吸引力，而不必假装能容纳所有人。成熟的第一个迹象，会是一则承认这一点的广告。

本批词根亮点：

• ingrained/grain：ingrained=深入纹理的=根深蒂固的，和 grain（纹理/谷粒）同根，木头的纹理深处=习惯难改

• dilapidated：di+lapid（石头），原意“石头散落”=建筑物损坏，lapis lazuli（青金石）同根

• sophisticated：来自 sophist（诡辩家），原意“被诡辩腐化的”，后演变为“复杂世故的”，philosophy（哲学）同根

• star-crossed：来自占星术，crossed by stars=星象不利=命运多舛，Shakespeare 在《罗密欧与朱丽叶》中创造

• infatuated：fatuus（愚蠢），infatuated=被愚弄而着迷的，fatuity（愚蠢）同根

• inured：in+ure（使用/工作），通过反复使用而习以为常=习惯于，manure（肥料=手工劳作）同根

• serrated：serra（锯子，拉丁），serrated=像锯一样有齿的，Sierra Nevada（内华达山脉=锯齿山）同根

• superannuated：super+annus（年），超过年龄=过了使用年限=过时的，annual（年度）同根

quiz.question: verified _______
quiz.explanation: 经过验证的，经过验证的账户。Her social media verified account had a blue checkmark. 她的社交媒体经过验证的账户有蓝色标记。 | ver->真（拉丁verus），verified->被证明为真的（cf. verify核实，veracity真实性，verdict裁决，aver断言） || 文化联想：微博蓝V最容易帮助记忆 verified：经过平台核实身份的账号可以说 **a verified account — “A blue V on Weibo marks a verified account whose identity has been checked by the platform.”**

quiz.question: unjustified _____
quiz.explanation: 不合理的，不合理的声明。The lawsuit was based on an unjustified claim. 这起诉讼基于不合理的声明。 | un->否定，just->正当（拉丁justus），unjustified->没有正当理由的（cf. justify证明正当，justice正义，adjust调整） || 文化联想：岳飞故事中“莫须有”常被用来指没有充分证据的罪名，可以说 **an unjustified accusation — “The charge remembered as ‘莫须有’ is often cited as an unjustified accusation made without solid evidence.”**

quiz.question: pied _______
quiz.explanation: 斑驳的，斑驳的鹡鸰。The pied wagtail is a common British bird. 斑驳的鹡鸰是常见的英国鸟类。 | pied->杂色的（来自magpie=喜鹊的黑白色），pied->有两种颜色斑块的（cf. pie馅饼=多种材料混合，piebald花斑马，Pied Piper花衣魔笛手） || 文化联想：大熊猫黑白两色块状分布的毛色很适合联想到 pied，可以说 **pied coloring — “The giant panda is instantly recognizable for its pied black-and-white coloring.”**

quiz.question: serried _____
quiz.explanation: 密集的，密集的队列。The soldiers stood in serried ranks. 士兵们站成密集的队列。 | serr->锁紧（拉丁serrare->锁），serried->紧密排列的（cf. series系列，serial连续的，insert插入=放入之间） || 文化联想：秦始皇兵马俑一个挨一个排成严整军阵的景象很适合联想到 serried，可以说 **serried ranks — “The Terracotta Warriors stand in serried ranks, row after row like an army frozen in time.”**

quiz.question: packed _______
quiz.explanation: 拥挤的，拥挤的体育场。The packed stadium roared with excitement. 拥挤的体育场充满兴奋的欢呼。 | pack->打包（古挪威pakki），packed->塞满的=拥挤的（cf. pack包裹，package包装，compact紧凑，impact冲击=打包进去） || 文化联想：春运时列车和候车大厅常常挤得满满当当，可以说 **a packed train — “During the Spring Festival travel rush, a packed train can be filled with passengers heading home for reunion.”**

quiz.question: henpecked _______
quiz.explanation: 怕老婆的，怕老婆的丈夫。The henpecked husband never made decisions alone. 怕老婆的丈夫从不独自做决定。 | hen->母鸡，pecked->啄，henpecked->被母鸡啄的=被老婆管的（cf. hen母鸡，peck啄，cf. under the thumb在拇指下=受控制） || 文化联想：四川方言里开玩笑说“耙耳朵”常指怕老婆、被妻子管得严的丈夫，可以说 **a henpecked husband — “In Sichuan slang, a ‘pa er duo’ jokingly refers to a henpecked husband who is bossed around by his wife.”**

quiz.question: wicked ____
quiz.explanation: 邪恶的，邪恶的行为。The villain committed a wicked deed. 恶棍犯下了邪恶的行为。 | wicca->巫师（古英语），wicked->像巫师一样邪恶的（cf. witch女巫，Wicca现代巫术，cf. wicked witch邪恶女巫） || 文化联想：传统故事里那些害人不眨眼、作恶多端的人物很适合用 wicked 来形容，可以说 **a wicked deed — “In old Chinese tales, a cruel villain who harms innocent people is condemned for every wicked deed he commits.”**

quiz.question: landlocked _______
quiz.explanation: 内陆的，内陆的国家。Switzerland is a landlocked country with no coastline. 瑞士是没有海岸线的内陆的国家。 | land->陆地，locked->锁住，landlocked->被陆地锁住的=内陆的（cf. lock锁，deadlock僵局，hemmed in被围困） || 文化联想：新疆深处亚洲大陆腹地、完全不临海，很适合帮助记忆 landlocked，可以说 **a landlocked region — “Xinjiang is a vast landlocked region in northwestern China, far from any ocean.”**

quiz.question: marked ___________
quiz.explanation: 显著的，显著的改进。There was a marked improvement in his grades. 他的成绩有显著的改进。 | mark->标记，marked->被明确标记出来的=显著的（cf. remarkable值得注意，marker标记，hallmark特征，benchmark基准） || 文化联想：深圳几十年间从边境小镇成长为国际化大城市，这种肉眼可见的巨大变化可以说 **a marked transformation — “Shenzhen underwent a marked transformation from a small border town into a global metropolis.”**

quiz.question: garbled _______
quiz.explanation: 混乱的，混乱的信息。The garbled message was impossible to understand. 混乱的信息无法理解。 | garble->筛选/曲解（阿拉伯语gharbala->筛），garbled->被混乱曲解的（cf. garbage垃圾=筛选后的废料，cf. garble original message歪曲原意） || 文化联想：“以讹传讹”最适合帮助记忆 garbled：消息一层层转述后会变得面目全非，可以说 **a garbled account — “The Chinese idiom 以讹传讹 describes how repeated retelling can turn a story into a garbled account of what actually happened.”**

quiz.question: unbridled _______
quiz.explanation: 不受约束的，不受约束的激情。His unbridled passion for music was evident. 他对音乐不受约束的激情是显而易见的。 | un->否定，bridle->马笼头，unbridled->没有马笼头约束的=放纵的（cf. bridle缰绳，rein控制，unrestrained不受约束） || 文化联想：“脱缰野马”就是没有缰绳约束、越跑越失控的形象，很适合联想到 unbridled，可以说 **unbridled energy — “The image of a runaway horse in 脱缰野马 vividly conveys unbridled energy that can no longer be restrained.”**

quiz.question: brindled ____

quiz.question: disheveled ____

quiz.question: muffled _____

quiz.question: unspoiled ______

quiz.question: unprincipled _____
quiz.explanation: 无原则的，无原则的恶棍。The unprincipled rogue would do anything for money. 无原则的恶棍会为钱做任何事。 | un->否定，principal->主要的/原则（拉丁princeps->第一），unprincipled->没有原则的（cf. principle原则，principal主要，prince王子） || 文化联想：“见利忘义”就是为了利益连原则和道义都可以丢掉，很适合联想到 unprincipled，可以说 **an unprincipled person — “The idiom 见利忘义 condemns an unprincipled person who abandons righteousness for profit.”**

quiz.question: dappled ________
quiz.explanation: 斑驳的，斑驳的阳光。Dappled sunlight filtered through the trees. 斑驳的阳光透过树木。 | dapple->斑点（古挪威depill->点），dappled->有明暗斑点的（cf. dapple gray苹果灰马，mottled有斑点的，speckled有斑点的） || 文化联想：竹林里阳光透过竹叶洒下明暗交错的小片光影，很适合联想到 dappled，可以说 **dappled sunlight — “In a bamboo grove, dappled sunlight falls through the leaves and creates shifting patches of light and shadow.”**

quiz.question: gnarled ____

quiz.question: settled _____

quiz.question: inflamed ______

quiz.question: mistimed ______

quiz.question: well-groomed __________

quiz.question: ____ informed

quiz.question: unenlightened ____

quiz.question: feigned _______

quiz.question: unfeigned _______

quiz.question: constrained _____
quiz.explanation: 勉强的，勉强的微笑。She gave a constrained smile at the bad joke. 她对这个糟糕的笑话露出勉强的微笑。 | con->共同，strain->拉紧（拉丁stringere），constrained->被紧紧绑住的=勉强的（cf. restrain约束，strict严格，constrict收缩，strain张力） || 文化联想：“强颜欢笑”就是心里并不高兴却硬挤出笑容，可以说 **a constrained smile — “The phrase 强颜欢笑 describes a constrained smile forced onto the face despite unhappiness.”**

quiz.question: sustained ______

quiz.question: ____ defined
quiz.explanation: 明确的，明确定义的。The project had well defined objectives. 该项目有明确定义的目标。 | de->设定，fine->边界（拉丁finis），defined->设定了边界=被定义的（cf. define定义，definite明确，finite有限，infinite无限） || 文化联想：“泾渭分明”用两水分界清楚来形容界限明确，很适合联想到 defined，可以说 **clearly defined boundaries — “The idiom 泾渭分明 evokes clearly defined boundaries, like two bodies of water whose colors remain visibly distinct.”**

quiz.question: ___ tined ____

quiz.question: impassioned ____

quiz.question: seasoned _______

quiz.question: biped ____
quiz.explanation: 两足动物的，两足动物的步态。Humans walk with a distinctive biped gait. 人类以独特的两足动物的步态行走。 | bi->两，ped->脚（拉丁pes），biped->有两只脚的（cf. quadruped四足，centipede百足虫，pedal踏板，pedestrian行人） || 文化联想：周口店北京人遗址最适合帮助记忆 biped：直立人的重要特征就是两足行走，可以说 **a biped hominin — “The Zhoukoudian fossils represent a biped hominin that walked upright on two legs.”**

quiz.question: damped ___________
quiz.explanation: 阻尼的，阻尼的振荡。The engineer designed a damped oscillation system. 工程师设计了阻尼的振荡系统。 | damp->潮湿/减弱（古挪威dampi->蒸汽），damped->被减弱的=阻尼的（cf. damp潮湿，dampen减弱，dampener减震器） || 文化联想：寺庙铜钟敲响后振动会越来越弱、钟声逐渐消失，很适合联想到 damped，可以说 **a damped vibration — “After a bronze temple bell is struck, its motion becomes a damped vibration as the ringing gradually fades.”**

quiz.question: untapped _________
quiz.explanation: 未开发的，未开发的潜力。The region has vast untapped potential. 该地区有巨大的未开发的潜力。 | un->否定，tap->开龙头/利用，untapped->龙头未开的=未被利用的（cf. tap水龙头，tap into利用，exploit开发，harness利用） || 文化联想：中国地方志和家谱中仍有大量材料尚未被充分整理利用，很适合联想到 untapped，可以说 **an untapped resource — “Thousands of local gazetteers and genealogies can remain an untapped resource for historical research.”**

quiz.question: ____-______ quadruped

quiz.question: vinegared _____
quiz.explanation: 醋味的，醋味的味道。The salad had a vinegared taste. 沙拉有醋味的味道。 | vin->葡萄酒（法语，拉丁vinum），egre->酸（法语aigre），vinegar->酸葡萄酒=醋（cf. wine葡萄酒，eager渴望=酸得流口水，vineyard葡萄园） || 文化联想：山西老陈醋浇在面食上会形成非常鲜明的酸醋味，很适合联想到 vinegared，可以说 **a vinegared taste — “A bowl of Shanxi noodles finished with mature vinegar has a distinctly vinegared taste.”**

quiz.question: lowbred ______

quiz.question: sacred ___
quiz.explanation: 神圣的，神圣的誓言。The monks took a sacred vow of silence. 僧侣们立下了神圣的誓言保持沉默。 | sacr->神圣（拉丁sacer），sacred->被奉献给神的=神圣的（cf. sacrifice牺牲，sacrilege亵渎，consecrate奉献，desecrate亵渎） || 文化联想：泰山在中国古代国家祭祀中具有极高的神圣地位，很适合联想到 sacred，可以说 **a sacred site — “Mount Tai was treated as a sacred site where emperors performed major state rituals.”**

quiz.question: kindred _______

quiz.question: checkered ____

quiz.question: improvised ______

quiz.explanation: 被低估的，被严重低估。The cost was grossly underestimated. 成本被严重低估。 | under->低于，estimate->估计（拉丁aestimare），underestimated->估计低于实际的（cf. estimate估计，esteem尊重，overestimate高估） || 文化联想：“骄兵必败”提醒人不能轻视对手，很适合联想到 underestimated，可以说 **an underestimated opponent — “The warning 骄兵必败 reflects the danger of an underestimated opponent: dismissing the other side can lead to defeat.”**

quiz.question: opinionated ______
quiz.explanation: 固执己见的，固执己见的立场。He took an opinionated stance on the issue. 他对这个问题采取了固执己见的立场。 | opinion->意见（拉丁opinio），opinionated->过分坚持自己意见的（cf. opinion意见，opine持有意见，pinion翅膀=观点支持） || 文化联想：“固执己见”形容一个人只认自己的看法、不愿听别人意见，很适合联想到 opinionated，可以说 **an opinionated person — “The idiom 固执己见 describes an opinionated person who clings to personal views and refuses to listen to others.”**

quiz.question: bloated ___________
quiz.explanation: 臃肿的，臃肿的官僚机构。The bloated bureaucracy needed reform. 臃肿的官僚机构需要改革。 | bloat->膨胀（古挪威blautr->软湿），bloated->过度膨胀的=臃肿的（cf. bloat膨胀，inflate充气，distended膨胀，obese肥胖） || 文化联想：“机构臃肿”形容部门层级太多、人员冗余，正好可以帮助记忆 bloated，可以说 **a bloated bureaucracy — “The expression 机构臃肿 describes a bloated bureaucracy with too many layers, offices, and redundant posts.”**

quiz.question: celebrated ______
quiz.explanation: 著名的，著名的艺术家。The celebrated artist displayed her work. 著名的艺术家展示了她的作品。 | celeber->著名（拉丁），celebrated->被广泛庆贺而著名的（cf. celebrate庆祝，celebrity名人，celebrity status名人地位） || 文化联想：李白在中国文学史上声名极盛，是最典型的 celebrated 人物之一，可以说 **a celebrated poet — “Li Bai is a celebrated poet whose fame has endured for more than a millennium.”**

quiz.question: serrated _____
quiz.explanation: 锯齿状的，锯齿状的刀。Use a serrated knife to cut the bread. 用锯齿状的刀切面包。 | serra->锯子（拉丁），serrated->像锯一样有齿的（cf. Sierra山脉=锯齿山，serration锯齿，saw锯子） || 文化联想：茶树叶片边缘常有一排细小的锯齿，很适合联想到 serrated，可以说 **a serrated leaf — “A fresh tea leaf often has a finely serrated edge, with tiny saw-like teeth along the margin.”**

quiz.question: saturated ___
quiz.explanation: 饱和的，饱和脂肪。Saturated fat should be limited in diet. 饮食中应限制饱和脂肪。 | satur->足够（拉丁satis），saturated->充分填满的=饱和的（cf. satiate满足，satisfy满足，insatiable贪得无厌，Saturday土星日=充足） || 文化联想：春节装饰常把大面积高纯度红色铺满门窗和街道，很适合联想到 saturated，可以说 **saturated red — “Traditional Lunar New Year decorations often use a saturated red that looks rich and intense.”**

quiz.question: sated ________
quiz.explanation: 满足的，满足的食欲。After the feast, everyone had a sated appetite. 盛宴后，每个人都有满足的食欲。 | satis->足够（拉丁），sated->被充分满足的（cf. satisfy满足，satiate使满足，saturate饱和，insatiable贪得无厌） || 文化联想：“饱汉不知饿汉饥”把已经吃饱的人和挨饿的人作对比，很适合联想到 sated，可以说 **the sated diner — “The proverb 饱汉不知饿汉饥 contrasts the sated diner with the hungry person to warn that comfort can make suffering hard to understand.”**

quiz.question: premeditated ______
quiz.explanation: 预谋的，预谋的谋杀。The crime was premeditated murder. 这起犯罪是预谋的谋杀。 | pre->提前，meditat->思考（拉丁meditari），premeditated->提前思考策划的（cf. meditate冥想，mediation调解，remedy补救） || 文化联想：荆轲刺秦在行动前准备地图、匕首并谋划接近秦王，很适合联想到 premeditated，可以说 **a premeditated attack — “Jing Ke’s attempt on the King of Qin was a premeditated attack prepared in advance with a hidden dagger and a forged map.”**

quiz.question: unpremeditated ___
quiz.explanation: 非预谋的，非预谋的行为。It was an unpremeditated act of passion. 这是激情的非预谋的行为。 | un->否定，premeditated->预谋的，unpremeditated->未经预谋的=非预谋的（cf. spontaneous自发，impulsive冲动，spur-of-the-moment一时冲动） || 文化联想：“脱口而出”就是没经过事先计划、话一下子从嘴里冒出来，很适合联想到 unpremeditated，可以说 **an unpremeditated remark — “A comment that slips out 脱口而出 is an unpremeditated remark, spoken without prior planning.”**

quiz.question: agitated _____
quiz.explanation: 激动的，激动的人群。The agitated crowd demanded answers. 激动的人群要求答案。 | agit->推动（拉丁agitare->驱使），agitated->被激烈推动的=激动的（cf. agitate激动，agitation鼓动，agitator鼓动者，agile敏捷） || 文化联想：“坐立不安”就是焦躁得坐也不是、站也不是，很适合联想到 agitated，可以说 **an agitated state — “The idiom 坐立不安 describes an agitated state in which a person is too anxious to sit or stand comfortably.”**

quiz.question: understated ________
quiz.explanation: 低调的，低调的优雅。The room had understated elegance. 房间有低调的优雅。 | under->低于，stated->表达的，understated->表达低于实际的=低调的（cf. understate低调表达，overstate夸大，understatement保守说法） || 文化联想：宋代水墨画往往不用浓艳装饰，而靠留白和克制营造含蓄之美，很适合联想到 understated，可以说 **understated elegance — “The restraint and empty space of a Song-dynasty ink painting can create understated elegance rather than flashy decoration.”**

quiz.question: graduated ___
quiz.explanation: 累进的，累进税。The country has a graduated tax system. 该国有累进税制度。 | gradu->步骤（拉丁gradus->阶梯），graduated->按阶梯分级的=累进的（cf. grade等级，gradual逐渐，gradient坡度，degrade降级） || 文化联想：“循序渐进”强调按阶段一步一步推进，很适合联想到 graduated，可以说 **a graduated approach — “The principle 循序渐进 favors a graduated approach, advancing step by step rather than changing everything at once.”**

quiz.question: superannuated _________
quiz.explanation: 过时的，过时的设备。The factory used superannuated equipment. 工厂使用过时的设备。 | super->超过，annu->年（拉丁annus），superannuated->超过年龄限制的=过时的（cf. annual年度，anniversary周年，annuity年金，biannual每两年） || 文化联想：中文里把老朽过气、早该退出舞台的人戏称为“老古董”，很适合联想到 superannuated，可以说 **a superannuated official — “An old bureaucrat who has long outlived his usefulness might be mocked as a superannuated official, an ‘老古董’ still occupying the post.”**

quiz.question: antiquated ______
quiz.explanation: 陈旧的，陈旧的系统。The antiquated system needed updating. 陈旧的系统需要更新。 | antiqu->古（拉丁antiquus），antiquated->变得过于古老的=陈旧的（cf. antique古董，antiquity古代，antiquarian古物研究者） || 文化联想：“还抱着老黄历不放”就是拿早已过时的老办法应付新情况，很适合联想到 antiquated，可以说 **an antiquated idea — “The expression 还抱着老黄历不放 mocks someone who clings to an antiquated idea long after circumstances have changed.”**

quiz.question: infatuated ___
quiz.explanation: 迷恋的，迷恋的粉丝。The infatuated fan followed the celebrity everywhere. 迷恋的粉丝到处跟着这位名人。 | in->使，fatuus->愚蠢（拉丁），infatuated->被愚弄而着迷的=迷恋的（cf. fatuous愚蠢，fatuity愚蠢，fanatic狂热者=fanum神庙） || 文化联想：“情人眼里出西施”最适合帮助记忆 infatuated：迷恋一个人时会觉得对方格外美好，可以说 **infatuated with someone — “The saying 情人眼里出西施 captures how someone infatuated with a lover sees beauty that others may not see.”**

quiz.question: cultivated _____
quiz.explanation: 有修养的，有修养的品味。He had cultivated taste in art. 他在艺术方面有有修养的品味。 | cultiv->耕作（拉丁colere->耕），cultivated->经过精心耕耘培养的（cf. culture文化，cultivate培养，agriculture农业，cult崇拜） || 文化联想：传统“君子”理想强调读书修身、举止有礼，最适合联想到 cultivated，可以说 **a cultivated gentleman — “The traditional ideal of the 君子 combines learning, self-discipline, and refined manners, making him a cultivated gentleman in the cultural sense.”**

quiz.question: ______ indebted
quiz.explanation: 负债的，深深负债。The company was deeply indebted. 公司深深负债。 | in->进入，debt->债务（拉丁debitum），indebted->欠债的/感激的（cf. debt债务，debit借方，due应付的，owe欠） || 文化联想：“滴水之恩，当涌泉相报”强调受人一点恩惠也要铭记回报，很适合联想到 indebted，可以说 **deeply indebted to someone — “The saying 滴水之恩，当涌泉相报 expresses feeling deeply indebted to someone even for a small kindness.”**

quiz.question: distracted _______
quiz.explanation: 分心的，分心的驾驶。Distracted driving causes many accidents. 分心的驾驶导致许多事故。 | dis->分开，tract->拉（拉丁trahere），distracted->被拉向不同方向=分心的（cf. distract分心，attract吸引，extract提取，tractor拖拉机） || 文化联想：“心不在焉”就是人虽然坐在这里，注意力却跑到别处去了，很适合联想到 distracted，可以说 **a distracted mind — “The idiom 心不在焉 describes a distracted mind whose attention is somewhere else even while the body is present.”**

quiz.question: dejected ____
quiz.explanation: 沮丧的，沮丧的表情。He had a dejected look after losing the game. 输掉比赛后，他有沮丧的表情。 | de->向下，ject->投掷（拉丁jacere），dejected->被向下投掷=沮丧的（cf. reject拒绝，project投影，inject注射，eject驱逐） || 文化联想：“垂头丧气”把失败后低着头、没有精神的样子直接画了出来，很适合联想到 dejected，可以说 **look dejected — “The idiom 垂头丧气 literally pictures someone hanging the head in discouragement and perfectly describes how a dejected person looks.”**

quiz.question: ______ collected
quiz.explanation: 镇定的，保持镇定。Despite the chaos, she managed to remain collected. 尽管一片混乱，她还是设法保持镇定。 | col->共同，lect->选择（拉丁legere），collected->把自己整合集中=镇定的（cf. collect收集，select选择，recollect回忆，intellect智力） || 文化联想：“镇定自若”就是别人都慌了，自己仍然神色如常、头脑清楚，很适合联想到 collected，可以说 **calm and collected — “The idiom 镇定自若 describes someone who remains calm and collected even when everyone else is panicking.”**
